publish_to: 'none'
version: 1.0.521+1

environment:
  sdk: ^3.12.2

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  # The local flutter_agent_harness package (pure Dart core + dart:io env).
  flutter_agent_harness:
    path: ../

  # The local fa_ui package: the Fa theme + provider/model settings widgets.
  fa_ui:
    path: ../packages/fa_ui
  # The extension panel's worker-relay transports + protocol (issue #34).
  # Path dep: fa_browser_agent ships inside the repo's browser_ext/ and is
  # compiled into the SW separately; the app only shares the wire types.
  fa_browser_agent:
    path: ../browser_ext/dart


  # The Office add-in bridge (issue #182): the outlook taskpane bundle
  # (FA_HOST=office) embeds the OfficeHostBridge + outlook.* mail tools
  # from this package; every other build tree-shakes them out.
  fa_office_agent:
    path: ../office_addin/dart

  # The local fa_llm package: the LLM config + Copilot device-flow types
  # the connect flow wires.
  fa_llm:
    path: ../packages/fa_llm

  # The DAP/1 hub client (hosted): powers the settings DAP-hub section —
  # the machine-shared `~/.dap` config, identity, and the connection probe.
  # IO-bound (dart:io WebSocket + files); web gets the honest stub.
  fa_hub_client: ^0.2.10

  # Mobile-friendly filesystem root and image picking.
  path_provider: ^2.1.6
  image_picker: ^1.2.3
  # Clipboard images for the composer's smart paste (Cmd/Ctrl+V).
  pasteboard: ^0.5.0
  # Image decode/encode for the Gemini adapter (PNG → JPEG conversion
  # strips alpha/EXIF that Gemini's vision encoder rejects).
  image: ^4.5.4

  # Load API keys and runtime config from .env for local dev/simulator runs.
  flutter_dotenv: ^6.0.1

  # JS apps platform: runs JavaScript widgets and renders them as native
  # Flutter UI (QuickJS via flutter_js on VM, web worker on web).
  # 0.4.154 ships the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`, >=
  # 0.4.127) that fa-craft 0.2.x probes for — older runtimes fall back to
  # the legacy scene3d path (slower, and not what fa-craft field testing
  # exercises) — plus jsr.openUrl + the webView node (gh-1235). 0.4.156
  # (gh-1341) carries upstream 9d57570: the flutter_js engine derives its
  # setupBridge channel list from JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels instead of
  # a hand-maintained copy, so `jsr.hostCall`/`jsr.capture` no longer hang
  # forever on JSC builds (voxel.attach probes → infinite spinner,
  # fa-craft → permanent legacy scene3d fallback at ~2 FPS).
  js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.156

  # The fa_widgets catalog validator — the SAME rule engine the catalog CI
  # runs (issue #1045): publish pre-flight imports it so a manifest that
  # passes on-device passes in CI, with byte-identical error strings.
  # publish_to: none upstream → git dep, sha-pinned for reproducibility.
  fa_widgets_tool:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/IstiN/fa_widgets.git
      ref: 3aa82cfd381e9b786fde363d7cde63cf31d1ef7a

  # TileProvider type for injecting offline map tiles (tests, custom hosts).
  flutter_map: ^8.2.2

  # SVG app icons (inline markup or apps/<id>/*.svg files).
  flutter_svg: ^2.3.0

  cupertino_icons: ^1.0.9
  flutter_chat_ui: ^2.11.1
  flutter_markdown: ^0.7.7+1
  re_highlight: ^0.0.3
  http: ^1.6.0
  cupertino_http: ^2.0.2
  uuid: ^4.6.0
  flutter_chat_core: ^2.9.0
  yaml: ^3.1.3
  # Sandbox-safe web URL strategy (issue #202): the OWA iframe strips
  # history.replaceState and the engine's default deep-link sync dies on it.
  flutter_web_plugins:
    sdk: flutter
  # Modern web bindings (package:web) for the history probe — dart:html is
  # deprecated by the analyzer.
  web: ^1.1.1

  # UI localization (gen-l10n, lib/l10n/*.arb → AppLocalizations).
  flutter_localizations:
    sdk: flutter
  intl: any

  # Myers diff used by the pure-Dart diff/patch sandbox builtins.
  diffutil_dart: ^4.0.1

  # Git support for the mobile sandbox: pure-Dart local porcelain (network clone
  # is implemented as a GitHub tarball fallback; full smart HTTP clone is a TODO).
  dart_git:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/GitJournal/dart-git.git
      ref: master

  path: ^1.9.0

  # package:file MemoryFileSystem for the web sandbox git store.
  file: ^7.0.1

  # WASM runtime used to run a uutils/ripgrep shell on iOS/Android/Web.
  wasm_run_flutter: ^0.1.0
  wasm_run: ^0.1.0+2

  # Pure-Dart inflate with exact stream-end tracking, used by git_smart_http
  # to parse packfiles (dart:io zlib cannot report the consumed length).
  # Its XZ/bzip2 decoders also back the sandbox xz/bzip2 -d builtins.
  archive: ^4.0.9

  # MD5/SHA digests for the sandbox md5sum/sha*sum builtins.
  crypto: ^3.0.3
  dartssh2: ^2.22.2

  # Network mode (issue #955): fa_network REST+WS client and the 'fanet1'
  # envelope crypto (X25519/HKDF/ChaCha20-Poly1305, DAP/1 recipe).
  cryptography: ^2.7.0
  web_socket_channel: ^2.4.0
  # Argon2id KDF for the passphrase-encrypted KeyWallet export (pure Dart,
  # web-safe); only the KDF is used, AEAD stays on package:cryptography.
  pointycastle: ^4.0.0

  # On-device Gemma 4 inference (iOS/Android via FFI, web via @litert-lm/core,
  # .litertlm engine). Imported only from lib/gemma/ behind conditional
  # imports — host tests never touch the plugin.
  flutter_gemma: ^1.5.2
  flutter_gemma_litertlm: ^1.3.1

  # Pinned explicitly because lib/gemma/gemma_web_registration_web.dart
  # imports them directly: dart2js release builds tree-shake the generated
  # web plugin registrant's platform-instance assignments out, so the Gemma
  # web path re-registers FlutterGemmaWeb and the SharedPreferences web impl
  # from its own retained code (see that file's docstring).
  shared_preferences_web: ^2.4.3
  shared_preferences_platform_interface: ^2.4.1

  # In-app HTML file preview on mobile/desktop (web uses an iframe instead —
  # see lib/ui/widgets/html_preview_web.dart).
  webview_flutter: ^4.14.1

  # Embedded web content for JS-app `webView` nodes (issue gh-1235): the
  # FaWebViewHost implementation over flutter_inappwebview (iOS/Android/
  # macOS; other platforms fall back to the renderer's placeholder).
  # 6.2.0-beta.3 is the first line whose Android implementation evaluates
  # under AGP 9 (1.1.3 calls getDefaultProguardFile('proguard-android.txt'),
  # which AGP 9 removed — the APK CI leg fails on it); the betas are one
  # coherent set (platform_interface 1.4.0-beta.3 + matching impls, per
  # upstream), so the umbrella moves as a whole. Return to ^6.1.x stable
  # once 6.2.0 stable ships.
  flutter_inappwebview: ^6.2.0-beta.3

  # Inline playback of sandbox-generated media in the chat (see
  # lib/ui/widgets/media_player.dart): audio plays from in-memory bytes,
  # video from a temp file (video is not supported in the web build).
  audioplayers: ^6.8.1
  video_player: ^2.13.0

  # Firebase: analytics across iOS, Android, macOS, and web. EXACT pins:
  # pubspec.lock IS now committed (gh-1265) and CI resolves with
  # --enforce-lockfile, but the exact pins stay as defense in depth — a
  # same-day pub release once pulled firebase_crashlytics 5.2.7 whose
  # firebase-ios-sdk 12.17.0 did not exist on SPM yet — the build died in
  # 'Could not resolve package dependencies' (build 80). Bump deliberately.
  firebase_core: 4.12.1
  firebase_analytics: 12.4.5

  # Opens the privacy policy link (onboarding privacy page) in the browser.
  url_launcher: ^6.3.1
  # Deep-link handling for mobile OAuth callbacks (fah://oauth/openrouter).
  app_links: ^6.4.0
  firebase_crashlytics: 5.2.6
  # WS channel abstraction for the fa_network realtime socket.
  stream_channel: ^2.1.0

dev_dependencies:
  # Mock seam for url_launcher in widget/golden tests.
  url_launcher_platform_interface: ^2.3.2
  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter
  integration_test:
    sdk: flutter
  flutter_lints: ^6.0.0
  flutter_launcher_icons: ^0.14.0
  # LatLng for the hand-built map canvas in the store screenshot goldens.
  latlong2: ^0.9.1
  # Fake WebViewPlatform for golden tests of lib/ui/widgets/html_preview_stub.dart.
  webview_flutter_platform_interface: ^2.15.1
  test: ^1.31.0
  # CLI visual tests (test/cli_visual/): real TerminalView rendering of the
  # Fa CLI running in a PTY — screenshots come from the actual xterm widget,
  # not a hand-rolled rasterizer.
  xterm: ^4.0.0
  pty2: ^0.5.3
  # omp REG parity legs (issue #810): the capture + fa-side visual tests
  # drive both CLIs through the same scripted OpenAI-compatible mock.
  fa_llm_mock:
    path: ../packages/fa_llm_mock

dependency_overrides:
  # fa_widgets_tool declares archive ^3.6.1 while the app needs ^4.0.9 (the
  # wasm/zip sandbox builtins). The override resolves the graph to 4.x; the
  # client only exercises validateWidgetDirectory, which never touches
  # archive — the packaging/pin-fetch code paths that do run in CI, not in
  # the app. ponytail: if a client path ever needs pin_fetcher, revisit.
  archive: ^4.0.9
  # (meta override removed with Flutter 3.47.4: the SDK now declares
  # meta ^1.18.3 and dart_tui 2.x declares ^1.19.0, so meta 1.19.0
  # resolves for both without an override.)
  freezed_annotation: ^3.1.0
  flutter_agent_memory: ^0.2.3
  fa_llm:
    path: ../packages/fa_llm
  # Same as the root pubspec_overrides.yaml: the vendored patched fork is
  # the renderer the real CLI runs; cli_visual tests compile its sources.
  # (composer fa_tui needs LineEditor, which the hosted 2.x predates.)
  dart_tui:
    path: ../vendor/dart_tui
  wasm_run:
    path: ../vendor/wasm_run
  wasm_run_flutter:
    path: ../vendor/wasm_run_flutter
  flutter_js:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js.git
      # fix-jscore-multi-instance: route sendMessage by executing context +
      # guard post-dispose evaluate. Stock 0.8.7 dispatches the shared native
      # sendMessage callback to the LAST created runtime, so coexisting JS
      # engines (launcher tiles + open apps) convert each other's JSValues
      # with the wrong JSContext — SIGSEGV in JSC::JSLock::lock once one of
      # them is disposed (TestFlight feedback-7).
      ref: 74a11bf6e7ab2721146cdc4a80e225115a8ccfe3
  # gh-1341: the js_widget_runtime git override (bd1e7c2) is gone —
  # hosted 0.4.156 (= upstream 9d57570, the flutter_js hostCall/capture
  # channel fix) is published, and the ^0.4.156 constraint resolves it.
  # flutter_inappwebview_macos 1.2.0-beta.3 declares a macOS 10.14 floor in
  # both its Package.swift and podspec, but its Swift marks
  # presentationAnchor(for:) @available(macOS 10.15, *) — the plugin fails to
  # compile at 10.14 on both the SwiftPM and CocoaPods paths (upstream bug,
  # still on master). Vendored verbatim with ONLY the deployment floor raised
  # to the app's 14.0 (vendor/flutter_inappwebview_macos/VENDORED.md). Drop
  # the override once upstream fixes the minimum.
  flutter_inappwebview_macos:
    path: ../vendor/flutter_inappwebview_macos
  # gh-1265: the umbrella's desktop implementations are pulled into every
  # native desktop build, but the app never uses the plugin on Linux or
  # Windows (createFaWebViewHost() in lib/apps/fa_webview_host.dart returns
  # null there — the renderer shows a placeholder). The real impls broke the
  # nightly desktop release legs: linux hard-requires the WPE WebKit system
  # library (absent from Ubuntu 24.04 entirely — libwpewebkit-1.0-dev is
  # jammy-only) and windows C++17-without-/await sources trip MSVC 14.51's
  # STL1011 on <experimental/coroutine>. Same-name stub overrides with NO
  # flutter: plugin: section (vendor/*_stub/VENDORED.md) register no native
  # code, returning both legs to the native surface they had when last
  # green. Guarded by test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart.
  flutter_inappwebview_linux:
    path: ../vendor/flutter_inappwebview_linux_stub
  flutter_inappwebview_windows:
    path: ../vendor/flutter_inappwebview_windows_stub

flutter:
  uses-material-design: true
  generate: true

  assets:
    - .env
    - assets/wasm/add.wasm
    - assets/wasm/coreutils.wasm
    - assets/wasm/rg.wasm
    - assets/wasm/find.wasm
    - assets/wasm/sed.wasm
    - assets/wasm/awk.wasm
    - assets/wasm/tar.wasm
    - assets/wasm/gzip.wasm
    - assets/wasm/zip.wasm
    - assets/wasm/python.wasm
    - assets/wasm/python_stdlib.zip
    - assets/wasm/qjs.wasm
    - assets/wasm/sqlite3.wasm
    - assets/wasm/lua.wasm
    - assets/wasm/wasi_hello.wasm
    - assets/wasm/LICENSE.coreutils
    - assets/wasm/LICENSE.rg
    - assets/wasm/LICENSE.findutils
    - assets/wasm/LICENSE.sed
    - assets/wasm/LICENSE.awk
    - assets/wasm/LICENSE.tar
    - assets/wasm/LICENSE.gzip
    - assets/wasm/LICENSE.zip
    - assets/wasm/LICENSE.python
    - assets/wasm/LICENSE.quickjs
    - assets/wasm/LICENSE.lua
    - assets/wasm/ATTRIBUTION.md
    - assets/fonts/

  fonts:
    # Inter (SIL OFL 1.1, assets/fonts/Inter-LICENSE.txt) — the app's UI
    # typeface on every platform, so the look is consistent and golden
    # screenshots are host-deterministic.
    - family: Inter
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf
        - asset: assets/fonts/Inter-Medium.ttf
          weight: 500
        - asset: assets/fonts/Inter-SemiBold.ttf
          weight: 600
        - asset: assets/fonts/Inter-Bold.ttf
          weight: 700
    # JetBrains Mono (SIL OFL 1.1) — code/terminal text.
    - family: JetBrainsMono
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/fonts/JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf
        - asset: assets/fonts/JetBrainsMono-Bold.ttf
          weight: 700

flutter_launcher_icons:
  # Android icons are NOT generated here: they derive from the iOS release
  # master via tool/generate_android_adaptive_icons.dart (issue #289) so
  # both platforms ship the identical icon (safe-zone adaptive foreground
  # + brand navy background). flutter_launcher_icons cannot express the
  # safe-zone padding, so android stays off here.
  android: false
  image_path: "assets/app_icon_source.png"
  ios: true
  remove_alpha_ios: true
  min_sdk_android: 21
  adaptive_icon_background: "#0b0f16"
  adaptive_icon_foreground: "assets/app_icon_source.png"
  macos:
    generate: true
  web:
    generate: false
  windows:
    generate: false
  linux:
    generate: false

blocks.text:
Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…
Let me start by exploring the working directory and reading the input context.

## PR Description

# gh-1341: Bump js_widget_runtime pin to 9d57570 / ^0.4.156 — flutter_js hostCall/capture channel fix (fa-craft lag, voxel-sandbox spinner)

## Description

## What

The pubspec git-override currently pins js_widget_runtime at `bd1e7c2`. Move it to **`9d57570`** (or hosted `^0.4.156` once CI publishes).

## Why (root cause of the mobile fa-craft/voxel-sandbox reports)

The flutter_js engine registered a hand-maintained `_bridgeChannels` list that was never updated when `__jsr_host_call` and `__jsr_capture` landed. flutter_js delivers `sendMessage` only to channels registered via `setupBridge` — messages on unregistered channels are silently dropped, so every `jsr.hostCall(...)` / `jsr.capture(...)` promise **hung forever** on JSC builds (the app uses FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend / JavascriptCoreRuntime on iOS+macOS):

- `voxel-sandbox`: first render gated behind the `voxel.attach` probe promise → **infinite spinner**;
- `fa-craft`: probe hangs → `nativeOn` stays null → permanent legacy scene3d fallback (full chunk mesh JSON re-sent every frame) → ~2 FPS and 16x mosaic-subdivided faces;
- the `jsr.openUrl` / `webView` wiring from #1235 rides on hostCall-shaped plumbing — same hang class.

Web worker + QuickJS engines dispatch all channels, which is why browser preview and the CLI never showed it. Bridge traffic stats on the phone confirmed it: zero `__jsr_host_call` across every 15 s window while RAF kept ticking.

## Fix (already upstream)

flutter_js_widget_runtime commit `9d57570`: `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` (union of the sync+async handler maps) is now the single source of truth and the flutter_js engine derives its `setupBridge` list from it; regression test asserts every channel sent by the bootstrap is dispatched. All quality gates green.

## Acceptance

- pubspec override ref updated (or switched to hosted `^0.4.156`), `flutter pub get`, lockfile committed.
- On an iOS/macOS build: `voxel-sandbox` renders (no spinner), `fa-craft` bridge stats show `__jsr_host_call` ≈ RAF counts and gameplay is smooth (native voxel path).

Assignee: ai-teammate (assign via UI if CLI fails).

environment:
  sdk: ^3.12.2

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  # The local flutter_agent_harness package (pure Dart core + dart:io env).
  flutter_agent_harness:
    path: ../

  # The local fa_ui package: the Fa theme + provider/model settings widgets.
  fa_ui:
    path: ../packages/fa_ui
  # The extension panel's worker-relay transports + protocol (issue #34).
  # Path dep: fa_browser_agent ships inside the repo's browser_ext/ and is
  # compiled into the SW separately; the app only shares the wire types.
  fa_browser_agent:
    path: ../browser_ext/dart


  # The Office add-in bridge (issue #182): the outlook taskpane bundle
  # (FA_HOST=office) embeds the OfficeHostBridge + outlook.* mail tools
  # from this package; every other build tree-shakes them out.
  fa_office_agent:
    path: ../office_addin/dart

  # The local fa_llm package: the LLM config + Copilot device-flow types
  # the connect flow wires.
  fa_llm:
    path: ../packages/fa_llm

  # The DAP/1 hub client (hosted): powers the settings DAP-hub section —
  # the machine-shared `~/.dap` config, identity, and the connection probe.
  # IO-bound (dart:io WebSocket + files); web gets the honest stub.
  fa_hub_client: ^0.2.10

  # Mobile-friendly filesystem root and image picking.
  path_provider: ^2.1.6
  image_picker: ^1.2.3
  # Clipboard images for the composer's smart paste (Cmd/Ctrl+V).
  pasteboard: ^0.5.0
  # Image decode/encode for the Gemini adapter (PNG → JPEG conversion
  # strips alpha/EXIF that Gemini's vision encoder rejects).
  image: ^4.5.4

  # Load API keys and runtime config from .env for local dev/simulator runs.
  flutter_dotenv: ^6.0.1

  # JS apps platform: runs JavaScript widgets and renders them as native
  # Flutter UI (QuickJS via flutter_js on VM, web worker on web).
  # 0.4.154 ships the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`, >=
  # 0.4.127) that fa-craft 0.2.x probes for — older runtimes fall back to

  # a hand-maintained copy, so `jsr.hostCall`/`jsr.capture` no longer hang
  # forever on JSC builds (voxel.attach probes → infinite spinner,

  js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.156

# gh-1341: Bump js_widget_runtime pin to 9d57570 / ^0.4.156 — flutter_js hostCall/capture channel fix (fa-craft lag, voxel-sandbox spinner)

## Description

## What

The pubspec git-override currently pins js_widget_runtime at `bd1e7c2`. Move it to **`9d57570`** (or hosted `^0.4.156` once CI publishes).

## Why (root cause of the mobile fa-craft/voxel-sandbox reports)

The flutter_js engine registered a hand-maintained `_bridgeChannels` list that was never updated when `__jsr_host_call` and `__jsr_capture` landed. flutter_js delivers `sendMessage` only to channels registered via `setupBridge` — messages on unregistered channels are silently dropped, so every `jsr.hostCall(...)` / `jsr.capture(...)` promise **hung forever** on JSC builds (the app uses FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend / JavascriptCoreRuntime on iOS+macOS):

- `voxel-sandbox`: first render gated behind the `voxel.attach` probe promise → **infinite spinner**;
- `fa-craft`: probe hangs → `nativeOn` stays null → permanent legacy scene3d fallback (full chunk mesh JSON re-sent every frame) → ~2 FPS and 16x mosaic-subdivided faces;
- the `jsr.openUrl` / `webView` wiring from #1235 rides on hostCall-shaped plumbing — same hang class.

Web worker + QuickJS engines dispatch all channels, which is why browser preview and the CLI never showed it. Bridge traffic stats on the phone confirmed it: zero `__jsr_host_call` across every 15 s window while RAF kept ticking.

## Fix (already upstream)

flutter_js_widget_runtime commit `9d57570`: `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` (union of the sync+async handler maps) is now the single source of truth and the flutter_js engine derives its `setupBridge` list from it; regression test asserts every channel sent by the bootstrap is dispatched. All quality gates green.

## Acceptance

- pubspec override ref updated (or switched to hosted `^0.4.156`), `flutter pub get`, lockfile committed.
- On an iOS/macOS build: `voxel-sandbox` renders (no spinner), `fa-craft` bridge stats show `__jsr_host_call` ≈ RAF counts and gameplay is smooth (native voxel path).

name: fa

environment:
  sdk: ^3.12.2

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  # The local flutter_agent_harness package (pure Dart core + dart:io env).
  flutter_agent_harness:
    path: ../

  # The local fa_ui package: the Fa theme + provider/model settings widgets.
  fa_ui:
    path: ../packages/fa_ui
  # The extension panel's worker-relay transports + protocol (issue #34).
  # Path dep: fa_browser_agent ships inside the repo's browser_ext/ and is
  # compiled into the SW separately; the app only shares the wire types.
  fa_browser_agent:
    path: ../browser_ext/dart


  # The Office add-in bridge (issue #182): the outlook taskpane bundle
  # (FA_HOST=office) embeds the OfficeHostBridge + outlook.* mail tools
  # from this package; every other build tree-shakes them out.
  fa_office_agent:
    path: ../office_addin/dart

  # The local fa_llm package: the LLM config + Copilot device-flow types
  # the connect flow wires.
  fa_llm:
    path: ../packages/fa_llm

  # The DAP/1 hub client (hosted): powers the settings DAP-hub section —
  # the machine-shared `~/.dap` config, identity, and the connection probe.
  # IO-bound (dart:io WebSocket + files); web gets the honest stub.
  fa_hub_client: ^0.2.10

  # Mobile-friendly filesystem root and image picking.
  path_provider: ^2.1.6
  image_picker: ^1.2.3
  # Clipboard images for the composer's smart paste (Cmd/Ctrl+V).
  pasteboard: ^0.5.0
  # Image decode/encode for the Gemini adapter (PNG → JPEG conversion
  # strips alpha/EXIF that Gemini's vision encoder rejects).
  image: ^4.5.4

  # Load API keys and runtime config from .env for local dev/simulator runs.
  flutter_dotenv: ^6.0.1

  # JS apps platform: runs JavaScript widgets and renders them as native
  # Flutter UI (QuickJS via flutter_js on VM, web worker on web).
  # 0.4.154 ships the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`, >=
  # 0.4.127) that fa-craft 0.2.x probes for — older runtimes fall back to
  # the legacy scene3d path (slower, and not what fa-craft field testing
  # exercises) — plus jsr.openUrl + the webView node (gh-1235). 0.4.156
  # (gh-1341) carries upstream 9d57570: the flutter_js engine derives its
  # setupBridge channel list from JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels instead of
  # a hand-maintained copy, so `jsr.hostCall`/`jsr.capture` no longer hang
  # forever on JSC builds (voxel.attach probes → infinite spinner,
  # fa-craft → permanent legacy scene3d fallback at ~2 FPS).
  js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.156

  # The fa_widgets catalog validator — the SAME rule engine the catalog CI
  # runs (issue #1045): publish pre-flight imports it so a manifest that
  # passes on-device passes in CI, with byte-identical error strings.

      url: https://github.com/IstiN/fa_widgets.git

  flutter_map: ^8.2.2

  flutter_svg: ^2.3.0

  flutter_chat_ui: ^2.11.1
  flutter_markdown: ^0.7.7+1
  re_highlight: ^0.0.3
  http: ^1.6.0
  cupertino_http: ^2.0.2
  uuid: ^4.6.0
  flutter_chat_core: ^2.9.0
  yaml: ^3.1.3
  # Sandbox-safe web URL strategy (issue #202): the OWA iframe strips
  # history.replaceState and the engine's default deep-link sync dies on it.
  flutter_web_plugins:
    sdk: flutter
  # Modern web bindings (package:web) for the history probe — dart:html is
  # deprecated by the analyzer.
  web: ^1.1.1

  # UI localization (gen-l10n, lib/l10n/*.arb → AppLocalizations).
  flutter_localizations:
    sdk: flutter
  intl: any

  # Myers diff used by the pure-Dart diff/patch sandbox builtins.
  diffutil_dart: ^4.0.1

  # Git support for the mobile sandbox: pure-Dart local porcelain (network clone
  # is implemented as a GitHub tarball fallback; full smart HTTP clone is a TODO).
  dart_git:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/GitJournal/dart-git.git
      ref: master

  path: ^1.9.0

  # package:file MemoryFileSystem for the web sandbox git store.
  file: ^7.0.1

  # WASM runtime used to run a uutils/ripgrep shell on iOS/Android/Web.
  wasm_run_flutter: ^0.1.0
  wasm_run: ^0.1.0+2

  # Pure-Dart inflate with exact stream-end tracking, used by git_smart_http

  archive: ^4.0.9

  crypto: ^3.0.3
  dartssh2: ^2.22.2

  # Network mode (issue #955): fa_network REST+WS client and the 'fanet1'
  # envelope crypto (X25519/HKDF/ChaCha20-Poly1305, DAP/1 recipe).
  cryptography: ^2.7.0
  web_socket_channel: ^2.4.0
  # Argon2id KDF for the passphrase-encrypted KeyWallet export (pure Dart,

  pointycastle: ^4.0.0

  # On-device Gemma 4 inference (iOS/Android via FFI, web via @litert-lm/core,
  # .litertlm engine). Imported only from lib/gemma/ behind conditional

  flutter_gemma: ^1.5.2
  flutter_gemma_litertlm: ^1.3.1

  shared_preferences_web: ^2.4.3

  webview_flutter: ^4.14.1

  flutter_inappwebview: ^6.2.0-beta.3

  # Inline playback of sandbox-generated media in the chat (see

  audioplayers: ^6.8.1
  video_player: ^2.13.0

  # Firebase: analytics across iOS, Android, macOS, and web. EXACT pins:

  firebase_analytics: 12.4.5

  url_launcher: ^6.3.1
  # Deep-link handling for mobile OAuth callbacks (fah://oauth/openrouter).

  # WS channel abstraction for the fa_network realtime socket.
  stream_channel: ^2.1.0

dev_dependencies:

  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter

  flutter_launcher_icons: ^0.14.0
  # LatLng for the hand-built map canvas in the store screenshot goldens.

  # Fake WebViewPlatform for golden tests of lib/ui/widgets/html_preview_stub.dart.
  webview_flutter_platform_interface: ^2.15…

# gh-1341: Bump js_widget_runtime pin to 9d57570 / ^0.4.156 — flutter_js hostCall/capture channel fix (fa-craft lag, voxel-sandbox spinner)

## Description

## What

The pubspec git-override currently pins js_widget_runtime at `bd1e7c2`. Move it to **`9d57570`** (or hosted `^0.4.156` once CI publishes).

## Why (root cause of the mobile fa-craft/voxel-sandbox reports)

The flutter_js engine registered a hand-maintained `_bridgeChannels` list that was never updated when `__jsr_host_call` and `__jsr_capture` landed. flutter_js delivers `sendMessage` only to channels registered via `setupBridge` — messages on unregistered channels are silently dropped, so every `jsr.hostCall(...)` / `jsr.capture(...)` promise **hung forever** on JSC builds (the app uses FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend / JavascriptCoreRuntime on iOS+macOS):

- `voxel-sandbox`: first render gated behind the `voxel.attach` probe promise → **infinite spinner**;
- `fa-craft`: probe hangs → `nativeOn` stays null → permanent legacy scene3d fallback (full chunk mesh JSON re-sent every frame) → ~2 FPS and 16x mosaic-subdivided faces;
- the `jsr.openUrl` / `webView` wiring from #1235 rides on hostCall-shaped plumbing — same hang class.

Web worker + QuickJS engines dispatch all channels, which is why browser preview and the CLI never showed it. Bridge traffic stats on the phone confirmed it: zero `__jsr_host_call` across every 15 s window while RAF kept ticking.

## Fix (already upstream)

flutter_js_widget_runtime commit `9d57570`: `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` (union of the sync+async handler maps) is now the single source of truth and the flutter_js engine derives its `setupBridge` list from it; regression test asserts every channel sent by the bootstrap is dispatched. All quality gates green.

## Acceptance

- pubspec override ref updated (or switched to hosted `^0.4.156`), `flutter pub get`, lockfile committed.
- On an iOS/macOS build: `voxel-sandbox` renders (no spinner), `fa-craft` bridge stats show `__jsr_host_call` ≈ RAF counts and gameplay is smooth (native voxel path).

Assignee: ai-teammate (assign via UI if CLI fails).

name: fa

environment:

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  # The local flutter_agent_harness package (pure Dart core + dart:io env).
  flutter_agent_harness:
    path: ../

  # The local fa_ui package: the Fa theme + provider/model settings widgets.
  fa_ui:
    path: ../packages/fa_ui

  # Path dep: fa_browser_agent ships inside the repo's browser_ext/ and is
  # compiled into the SW separately; the app only shares the wire types.
  fa_browser_agent:
    path: ../browser_ext/dart


  # The Office add-in bridge (issue #182): the outlook taskpane bundle
  # (FA_HOST=office) embeds the OfficeHostBridge + outlook.* mail tools
  # from this package; every other build tree-shakes them out.
  fa_office_agent:
    path: ../office_addin/dart

  # The local fa_llm package: the LLM config + Copilot device-flow types
  # the connect flow wires.
  fa_llm:
    path: ../packages/fa_llm

  # The DAP/1 hub client (hosted): powers the settings DAP-hub section —
  # the machine-shared `~/.dap` config, identity, and the connection probe.
  # IO-bound (dart:io WebSocket + files); web gets the honest stub.
  fa_hub_client: ^0.2.10

  path_provider: ^2.1.6
  image_picker: ^1.2.3

  pasteboard: ^0.5.0

  image: ^4.5.4

  # Load API keys and runtime config from .env for local dev/simulator runs.
  flutter_dotenv: ^6.0.1

  # JS apps platform: runs JavaScript widgets and renders them as native
  # Flutter UI (QuickJS via flutter_js on VM, web worker on web).
  # 0.4.154 ships the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`, >=
  # 0.4.127) that fa-craft 0.2.x probes for — older runtimes fall back to
  # the legacy scene3d path (slower, and not what fa-craft field testing
  # exercises) — plus jsr.openUrl + the webView node (gh-1235). 0.4.156
  # (gh-1341) carries upstream 9d57570: the flutter_js engine derives its
  # setupBridge channel list from JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels instead of
  # a hand-maintained copy, so `jsr.hostCall`/`jsr.capture` no longer hang

  # fa-craft → permanent legacy scene3d fallback at ~2 FPS).

  flutter_chat_ui: ^2.11.1
  flutter_markdown: ^0.7.7+1

  http: ^1.6.0
  cupertino_http: ^2.0.2

  web: ^1.1.1

  # UI localization (gen-l10n, lib/l10n/*.arb → AppLocalizations).

  # Myers diff used by the pure-Dart diff/patch sandbox builtins.

  # Git support for the mobile sandbox: pure-Dart local porcelain (network clone

  dart_git:

  webview_flutter: ^4.14.1

  flutter_inappwebview: ^6.2.0-beta.3

  # Inline playback of sandbox-generated media in the chat (see

  audioplayers: ^6.8.1
  video_player: ^2.13.0

  # Firebase: analytics across iOS, Android, macOS, and web. EXACT pins:

  firebase_analytics: 12.4.5

  url_launcher: ^6.3.1
  # Deep-link handling for mobile OAuth callbacks (fah://oauth/openrouter).
  app_links: ^6.4.0
  firebase_crashlytics: 5.2.6
  # WS channel abstraction for the fa_network realtime socket.
  stream_channel: ^2.1.0

  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter

  flutter_launcher_icons: ^0.14.0
  # LatLng for the hand-built map canvas in the store screenshot goldens.

  # Fake WebViewPlatform for golden tests of lib/ui/widgets/html_preview_stub.dart.
  webview_flutter_platform_interface: ^2.15…

# gh-1341: Bump js_widget_runtime pin to 9d57570 / ^0.4.156 — flutter_js hostCall/capture channel fix (fa-craft lag, voxel-sandbox spinner)

## Description

## What

The pubspec git-override currently pins js_widget_runtime at `bd1e7c2`. Move it to **`9d57570`** (or hosted `^0.4.156` once CI publishes).

## Why (root cause of the mobile fa-craft/voxel-sandbox reports)

The flutter_js engine registered a hand-maintained `_bridgeChannels` list that was never updated when `__jsr_host_call` and `__jsr_capture` landed. flutter_js delivers `sendMessage` only to channels registered via `setupBridge` — messages on unregistered channels are silently dropped, so every `jsr.hostCall(...)` / `jsr.capture(...)` promise **hung forever** on JSC builds (the app uses FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend / JavascriptCoreRuntime on iOS+macOS):

- `voxel-sandbox`: first render gated behind the `voxel.attach` probe promise → **infinite spinner**;
- `fa-craft`: probe hangs → `nativeOn` stays null → permanent legacy scene3d fallback (full chunk mesh JSON re-sent every frame) → ~2 FPS and 16x mosaic-subdivided faces;
- the `jsr.openUrl` / `webView` wiring from #1235 rides on hostCall-shaped plumbing — same hang class.

Web worker + QuickJS engines dispatch all channels, which is why browser preview and the CLI never showed it. Bridge traffic stats on the phone confirmed it: zero `__jsr_host_call` across every 15 s window while RAF kept ticking.

## Fix (already upstream)

flutter_js_widget_runtime commit `9d57570`: `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` (union of the sync+async handler maps) is now the single source of truth and the flutter_js engine derives its `setupBridge` list from it; regression test asserts every channel sent by the bootstrap is dispatched. All quality gates green.

## Acceptance

- pubspec override ref updated (or switched to hosted `^0.4.156`), `flutter pub get`, lockfile committed.
- On an iOS/macOS build: `voxel-sandbox` renders (no spinner), `fa-craft` bridge stats show `__jsr_host_call` ≈ RAF counts and gameplay is smooth (native voxel path).

Assignee: ai-teammate (assign via UI if CLI fails).

  # compiled into the SW separately; the app only shares the wire types.
  fa_browser_agent:

  fa_office_agent:
    path: ../office_addin/dart

  fa_llm:
    path: ../packages/fa_llm

  # The DAP/1 hub client (hosted): powers the settings DAP-hub section —
  # the machine-shared `~/.dap` config, identity, and the connection probe.

  image: ^4.5.4

  # (gh-1341) carries upstream 9d57570: the flutter_js engine derives its

That's a test-only helper; a failure would be a crash rather than silent pass. Minor.

2. **The test asserting `description['url'] == 'https://pub.dev'`** — pub may render the url field as `https://pub.dev` in the lockfile on some pub versions; actually hosted source entries in pubspec.lock typically don't include a `url` field when it's the default host. 7. **Potential issue — `flutter_js` override still git-pinned**: The flutter_js package remains a git override (74a11bf). The fix upstream (9d57570) is in flutter_js_widget_runtime, which derives setupBridge list from `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels`, and it needs flutter_js to call setupBridge with those channels. Since js_widget_runtime 0.4.156 depends on flutter_js — with the app overriding flutter_js to a specific git ref (74a11bf, the JSC multi-instance fix) — the question: does js_widget_runtime 0.4.156 work with that older/newer flutter_js commit? The PR says they verified `handledChannels` grep in cached package source and CI is green (unit gate 9189 passed, flutter analyze parity). But CI on Linux can't validate the JSC path. The fix: "the flutter_js engine derives its setupBridge list from handledChannels" — i.e., in flutter_js_widget_runtime, when creating the engine, it now passes the full channel list. So it's the js_widget_runtime side that changed; flutter_js API (setupBridge with list) presumably unchanged. # gh-1341: Bump js_widget_runtime pin to 9d57570 / ^0.4.156 — flutter_js hostCall/capture channel fix (fa-craft lag, voxel-sandbox spinner)

## Description

## What

The pubspec git-override currently pins js_widget_runtime at `bd1e7c2`. Move it to **`9d57570`** (or hosted `^0.4.156` once CI publishes).

## Why (root cause of the mobile fa-craft/voxel-sandbox reports)

The flutter_js engine registered a hand-maintained `_bridgeChannels` list that was never updated when `__jsr_host_call` and `__jsr_capture` landed. flutter_js delivers `sendMessage` only to channels registered via `setupBridge` — messages on unregistered channels are silently dropped, so every `jsr.hostCall(...)` / `jsr.capture(...)` promise **hung forever** on JSC builds (the app uses FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend / JavascriptCoreRuntime on iOS+macOS):

- `voxel-sandbox`: first render gated behind the `voxel.attach` probe promise → **infinite spinner**;
- `fa-craft`: probe hangs → `nativeOn` stays null → permanent legacy scene3d fallback (full chunk mesh JSON re-sent every frame) → ~2 FPS and 16x mosaic-subdivided faces;
- the `jsr.openUrl` / `webView` wiring from #1235 rides on hostCall-shaped plumbing — same hang class.

Web worker + QuickJS engines dispatch all channels, which is why browser preview and the CLI never showed it. Bridge traffic stats on the phone confirmed it: zero `__jsr_host_call` across every 15 s window while RAF kept ticking.

## Fix (already upstream)

flutter_js_widget_runtime commit `9d57570`: `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` (union of the sync+async handler maps) is now the single source of truth and the flutter_js engine derives its `setupBridge` list from it; regression test asserts every channel sent by the bootstrap is dispatched. All quality gates green.

## Acceptance

- pubspec override ref updated (or switched to hosted `^0.4.156`), `flutter pub get`, lockfile committed.
- On an iOS/macOS build: `voxel-sandbox` renders (no spinner), `fa-craft` bridge stats show `__jsr_host_call` ≈ RAF counts and gameplay is smooth (native voxel path).

Assignee: ai-teammate (assign via UI if CLI fails).

The pubspec.yaml change looks consistent. Now let me check the new test file in full, and the changed nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart context. Also read AGENTS.md sections relevant to review, particularly coding conventions.

Key review considerations:

1. **The `pubVersion` function in the new test** — it's a hand-rolled version comparator. `int.parse` on parts — what if a version has a pre-release suffix or build metadata like `0.4.156+1`? For `pubspec.lock` entries the version is a plain `x.y.z` string, so probably fine. But if the version had fewer/more parts or non-numeric parts, `int.parse` would throw. That's a test-only helper; a failure would be a crash rather than silent pass. Minor.

   Actually wait — `pubVersion` shifting: `(parts[0] << 20) | (parts[1] << 10) | parts[2]` — for 0.4.156 vs 0.4.1000? part[2] max 1023. 156 < 1023 fine. If minor > 1023 unlikely. Fine for the domain. Dart `int` is 64-bit, so no overflow concerns.

2. **The test asserting `description['url'] == 'https://pub.dev'`** — pub may render the url field as `https://pub.dev` in the lockfile on some pub versions; actually hosted source entries in pubspec.lock typically don't include a `url` field when it's the default host. Wait — the diff shows the lockfile entry HAS `url: "https://pub.dev"`. Let me check: in the lockfile diff:
   ```yaml
   js_widget_runtime:
     dependency: "direct main"
     description:
       name: js_widget_runtime
       sha256: "18f7e97d..."
       url: "https://pub.dev"
     source: hosted
     version: "0.4.156"
   ```
   Yes, newer pub versions include the url field. OK so the test asserts the same. Fine.

3. **Where is the test run from?** The test reads `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` with a relative path — so it must be run from the repo root (`dart test/jsr_host_call_pin_guard_test.dart` from root). The PR description says exactly that. But is this repo-root test suite run with the repo root as CWD? Root package is `flutter_agent_harness` at root, tests run from root. OK. But wait — does the root package's `dart test` include the `yaml` package? The test imports `package:yaml/yaml.dart`. Let me check root pubspec for yaml dependency. The root pubspec.yaml — I should check. Also `package:test/test.dart`.

4. **Also `flutter_app/test/` vs root `test/`** — the new test is at root `test/jsr_host_call_pin_guard_test.dart`. Existing similar guards: `test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart` at root, and `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart` — let me check the pattern to confirm they read flutter_app paths relative to root.

5. **CI enforcement**: does CI run root `dart test` fully? If the test is at root and CI runs the full suite, the guard runs. But the guard is also described as "TDD: red before the change". Fine.

6. **Lockfile drift**: pubspec.lock committed and CI uses `--enforce-lockfile`. The constraint `^0.4.156` and lockfile pinned 0.4.156 hosted. Fine.

7. **Potential issue — `flutter_js` override still git-pinned**: The flutter_js package remains a git override (74a11bf). The fix upstream (9d57570) is in flutter_js_widget_runtime, which derives setupBridge list from `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels`, and it needs flutter_js to call setupBridge with those channels. Since js_widget_runtime 0.4.156 depends on flutter_js — with the app overriding flutter_js to a specific git ref (74a11bf, the JSC multi-instance fix) — the question: does js_widget_runtime 0.4.156 work with that older/newer flutter_js commit? If 0.4.156's bridge logic requires a newer flutter_js than 74a11bf, there could be a mismatch. The PR says they verified `handledChannels` grep in cached package source and CI is green (unit gate 9189 passed, flutter analyze parity). But CI on Linux can't validate the JSC path. However, the guard test doesn't check flutter_js version. This is a possible IMPORTANT finding: the flutter_js git override pins a specific commit that may predate/miss whatever glue the fix needs; but the fix is in js_widget_runtime (derives channel list from its own handledChannels and calls flutter_js's setupBridge API), so as long as flutter_js 74a11bf has setupBridge with a channel-list parameter, it works. Actually the root cause per the ticket: "flutter_js delivers sendMessage only to channels registered via setupBridge — messages on unregistered channels are silently dropped". The fix: "the flutter_js engine derives its setupBridge list from handledChannels" — i.e., in flutter_js_widget_runtime, when creating the engine, it now passes the full channel list. So it's the js_widget_runtime side that changed; flutter_js API (setupBridge with list) presumably unchanged. Can't verify deeply without the package source; maybe check if the package is cached in the runner? Let me look for pub cache.

Let me check whether js_widget_runtime 0.4.156 source is available in the pub cache to verify claims. Also verify the sha256 matches pub.dev? That'd require network. I can check `~/.pub-cache`.

SUGGESTION level. Actually, wait: could there be a scenario where a legit future version string breaks this? Pub versions are always numeric triple + optional prerelease/build. If the lockfile pins e.g. `0.5.0-dev.1`, the test would throw FormatException → test fails with an unhelpful message. Minor robustness nit, SUGGESTION.

# gh-1341: Bump js_widget_runtime pin to 9d57570 / ^0.4.156 — flutter_js hostCall/capture channel fix (fa-craft lag, voxel-sandbox spinner)

## Description

## What

The pubspec git-override currently pins js_widget_runtime at `bd1e7c2`. Move it to **`9d57570`** (or hosted `^0.4.156` once CI publishes).

## Why (root cause of the mobile fa-craft/voxel-sandbox reports)

The flutter_js engine registered a hand-maintained `_bridgeChannels` list that was never updated when `__jsr_host_call` and `__jsr_capture` landed. flutter_js delivers `sendMessage` only to channels registered via `setupBridge` — messages on unregistered channels are silently dropped, so every `jsr.hostCall(...)` / `jsr.capture(...)` promise **hung forever** on JSC builds (the app uses FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend / JavascriptCoreRuntime on iOS+macOS):

- `voxel-sandbox`: first render gated behind the `voxel.attach` probe promise → **infinite spinner**;
- `fa-craft`: probe hangs → `nativeOn` stays null → permanent legacy scene3d fallback (full chunk mesh JSON re-sent every frame) → ~2 FPS and 16x mosaic-subdivided faces;
- the `jsr.openUrl` / `webView` wiring from #1235 rides on hostCall-shaped plumbing — same hang class.

Web worker + QuickJS engines dispatch all channels, which is why browser preview and the CLI never showed it. Bridge traffic stats on the phone confirmed it: zero `__jsr_host_call` across every 15 s window while RAF kept ticking.

## Fix (already upstream)

flutter_js_widget_runtime commit `9d57570`: `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` (union of the sync+async handler maps) is now the single source of truth and the flutter_js engine derives its `setupBridge` list from it; regression test asserts every channel sent by the bootstrap is dispatched. All quality gates green.

## Acceptance

- pubspec override ref updated (or switched to hosted `^0.4.156`), `flutter pub get`, lockfile committed.
- On an iOS/macOS build: `voxel-sandbox` renders (no spinner), `fa-craft` bridge stats show `__jsr_host_call` ≈ RAF counts and gameplay is smooth (native voxel path).

Assignee: ai-teammate (assign via UI if CLI fails).

  fa_browser_agent:
    path: ../browser_ext/dart

    path: ../office_addin/dart

  fa_llm:
    path: ../packages/fa_llm

  # the machine-shared `~/.dap` config, identity, and the connection probe.

  fa_hub_client: ^0.2.10

  # setupBridge channel list from JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels instead of
  # a hand-maintained copy, so `jsr.hostCall`/`jsr.capture` no longer hang

# gh-1341: Bump js_widget_runtime pin to 9d57570 / ^0.4.156 — flutter_js hostCall/capture channel fix (fa-craft lag, voxel-sandbox spinner)

## Description

## What

The pubspec git-override currently pins js_widget_runtime at `bd1e7c2`. Move it to **`9d57570`** (or hosted `^0.4.156` once CI publishes).

## Why (root cause of the mobile fa-craft/voxel-sandbox reports)

The flutter_js engine registered a hand-maintained `_bridgeChannels` list that was never updated when `__jsr_host_call` and `__jsr_capture` landed. flutter_js delivers `sendMessage` only to channels registered via `setupBridge` — messages on unregistered channels are silently dropped, so every `jsr.hostCall(...)` / `jsr.capture(...)` promise **hung forever** on JSC builds (the app uses FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend / JavascriptCoreRuntime on iOS+macOS):

- `voxel-sandbox`: first render gated behind the `voxel.attach` probe promise → **infinite spinner**;
- `fa-craft`: probe hangs → `nativeOn` stays null → permanent legacy scene3d fallback (full chunk mesh JSON re-sent every frame) → ~2 FPS and 16x mosaic-subdivided faces;
- the `jsr.openUrl` / `webView` wiring from #1235 rides on hostCall-shaped plumbing — same hang class.

Web worker + QuickJS engines dispatch all channels, which is why browser preview and the CLI never showed it. Bridge traffic stats on the phone confirmed it: zero `__jsr_host_call` across every 15 s window while RAF kept ticking.

## Fix (already upstream)

flutter_js_widget_runtime commit `9d57570`: `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` (union of the sync+async handler maps) is now the single source of truth and the flutter_js engine derives its `setupBridge` list from it; regression test asserts every channel sent by the bootstrap is dispatched. All quality gates green.

## Acceptance

- pubspec override ref updated (or switched to hosted `^0.4.156`), `flutter pub get`, lockfile committed.
- On an iOS/macOS build: `voxel-sandbox` renders (no spinner), `fa-craft` bridge stats show `__jsr_host_call` ≈ RAF counts and gameplay is smooth (native voxel path).

name: fa

environment:
  sdk: ^3.12.2

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  # The local flutter_agent_harness package (pure Dart core + dart:io env).
  flutter_agent_harness:
    path: ../

  # The local fa_ui package: the Fa theme + provider/model settings widgets.
  fa_ui:
    path: ../packages/fa_ui
  # The extension panel's worker-relay transports + protocol (issue #34).
  # Path dep: fa_browser_agent ships inside the repo's browser_ext/ and is
  # compiled into the SW separately; the app only shares the wire types.
  fa_browser_agent:
    path: ../browser_ext/dart


  # The Office add-in bridge (issue #182): the outlook taskpane bundle
  # (FA_HOST=office) embeds the OfficeHostBridge + outlook.* mail tools
  # from this package; every other build tree-shakes them out.
  fa_office_agent:
    path: ../office_addin/dart

  # The local fa_llm package: the LLM config + Copilot device-flow types
  # the connect flow wires.
  fa_llm:
    path: ../packages/fa_llm

  # The DAP/1 hub client (hosted): powers the settings DAP-hub section —
  # the machine-shared `~/.dap` config, identity, and the connection probe.
  # IO-bound (dart:io WebSocket + files); web gets the honest stub.
  fa_hub_client: ^0.2.10

  # Mobile-friendly filesystem root and image picking.
  path_provider: ^2.1.6
  image_picker: ^1.2.3
  # Clipboard images for the composer's smart paste (Cmd/Ctrl+V).
  pasteboard: ^0.5.0
  # Image decode/encode for the Gemini adapter (PNG → JPEG conversion
  # strips alpha/EXIF that Gemini's vision encoder rejects).
  image: ^4.5.4

  # Load API keys and runtime config from .env for local dev/simulator runs.
  flutter_dotenv: ^6.0.1

  # JS apps platform: runs JavaScript widgets and renders them as native
  # Flutter UI (QuickJS via flutter_js on VM, web worker on web).
  # 0.4.154 ships the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`, >=
  # 0.4.127) that fa-craft 0.2.x probes for — older runtimes fall back to
  # the legacy scene3d path (slower, and not what fa-craft field testing
  # exercises) — plus jsr.openUrl + the webView node (gh-1235). 0.4.156
  # (gh-1341) carries upstream 9d57570: the flutter_js engine derives its
  # setupBridge channel list from JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels instead of
  # a hand-maintained copy, so `jsr.hostCall`/`jsr.capture` no longer hang
  # forever on JSC builds (voxel.attach probes → infinite spinner,
  # fa-craft → permanent legacy scene3d fallback at ~2 FPS).
  js_widget_runtime: ^0.4.156

  # The fa_widgets catalog validator — the SAME rule engine the catalog CI
  # runs (issue #1045): publish pre-flight imports it so a manifest that
  # passes on-device passes in CI, with byte-identical error strings.

  flutter_map: ^8.2.2

  flutter_svg: ^2.3.0

  flutter_chat_ui: ^2.11.1
  flutter_markdown: ^0.7.7+1
  re_highlight: ^0.0.3
  http: ^1.6.0
  cupertino_http: ^2.0.2
  uuid: ^4.6.0
  flutter_chat_core: ^2.9.0
  yaml: ^3.1.3
  # Sandbox-safe web URL strategy (issue #202): the OWA iframe strips
  # history.replaceState and the engine's default deep-link sync dies on it.
  flutter_web_plugins:
    sdk: flutter
  # Modern web bindings (package:web) for the history probe — dart:html is
  # deprecated by the analyzer.
  web: ^1.1.1

  # UI localization (gen-l10n, lib/l10n/*.arb → AppLocalizations).
  flutter_localizations:
    sdk: flutter
  intl: any

  # Myers diff used by the pure-Dart diff/patch sandbox builtins.
  diffutil_dart: ^4.0.1

  # Git support for the mobile sandbox: pure-Dart local porcelain (network clone
  # is implemented as a GitHub tarball fallback; full smart HTTP clone is a TODO).
  dart_git:
    git:

  path: ^1.9.0

  file: ^7.0.1

  # WASM runtime used to run a uutils/ripgrep shell on iOS/Android/Web.
  wasm_run_flutter: ^0.1.0
  wasm_run: ^0.1.0+2

  crypto: ^3.0.3

  cryptography: ^2.7.0
  web_socket_channel: ^2.4.0

  pointycastle: ^4.0.0

  # On-device Gemma 4 inference (iOS/Android via FFI, web via @litert-lm/core,

  flutter_gemma: ^1.5.2
  flutter_gemma_litertlm: ^1.3.1

  shared_preferences_web: ^2.4.3

  webview_flutter: ^4.14.1

  flutter_inappwebview: ^6.2.0-beta.3

  # Inline playback of sandbox-generated media in the chat (see
  # lib/ui/widgets/media_player.dart): audio plays from in-memory bytes,
  # video from a temp file (video is not supported in the web build).
  audioplayers: ^6.8.1
  video_player: ^2.13.0

  # Firebase: analytics across iOS, Android, macOS, and web. EXACT pins:
  # pubspec.lock IS now committed (gh-1265) and CI resolves with
  # --enforce-lockfile, but the exact pins stay as defense in depth — a
  # same-day pub release once pulled firebase_crashlytics 5.2.7 whose
  # firebase-ios-sdk 12.17.0 did not exist on SPM yet — the build died in

  firebase_core: 4.12.1
  firebase_analytics: 12.4.5

  # Opens the privacy policy link (onboarding privacy page) in the browser.
  url_launcher: ^6.3.1
  # Deep-link handling for mobile OAuth callbacks (fah://oauth/openrouter).
  app_links: ^6.4.0
  firebase_crashlytics: 5.2.6
  # WS channel abstraction for the fa_network realtime socket.
  stream_channel: ^2.1.0

dev_dependencies:
  # Mock seam for url_launcher in widget/golden tests.

  flutter_test:
    sdk: flutter
  integration_test:

  flutter_launcher_icons: ^0.14.0
  # LatLng for the hand-built map canvas in the store screenshot goldens.

  # Fake WebViewPlatform for golden tests of lib/ui/widgets/html_preview_stub.dart.
  webview_flutter_platform_interface: ^2.15…

Switched `flutter_app`'s `js_widget_runtime` from the git pin `bd1e7c2` (0.4.154) to **hosted `^0.4.156`** — v0.4.156 = upstream `9d57570` (flutter_js bridge registers every `__jsr_*` channel via `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels`), so `jsr.hostCall`/`jsr.capture` no longer hang on JSC (iOS/macOS voxel spinner, fa-craft scene3d fallback). - Dropped the `dependency_overrides` git entry entirely — pubspec's own comment documented "drop the override once hosted lands", and hosted 0.4.156 is published and verified to contain `9d57570` (checked the `v0.4.156` tag ancestry; also grepped `handledChannels` in the cached package source).

- Updated stale pin references: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/js-apps.md`, `test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart` comment.
- Side benefit: one fewer git-dependency mirror clone in `flutter pub get` (the gh-1310 network-roulette class).

# gh-1341: Bump js_widget_runtime pin to 9d57570 / ^0.4.156 — flutter_js hostCall/capture channel fix (fa-craft lag, voxel-sandbox spinner)

## Description

## What

The pubspec git-override currently pins js_widget_runtime at `bd1e7c2`. Move it to **`9d57570`** (or hosted `^0.4.156` once CI publishes).

## Why (root cause of the mobile fa-craft/voxel-sandbox reports)

The flutter_js engine registered a hand-maintained `_bridgeChannels` list that was never updated when `__jsr_host_call` and `__jsr_capture` landed. flutter_js delivers `sendMessage` only to channels registered via `setupBridge` — messages on unregistered channels are silently dropped, so every `jsr.hostCall(...)` / `jsr.capture(...)` promise **hung forever** on JSC builds (the app uses FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend / JavascriptCoreRuntime on iOS+macOS):

- `voxel-sandbox`: first render gated behind the `voxel.attach` probe promise → **infinite spinner**;
- `fa-craft`: probe hangs → `nativeOn` stays null → permanent legacy scene3d fallback (full chunk mesh JSON re-sent every frame) → ~2 FPS and 16x mosaic-subdivided faces;
- the `jsr.openUrl` / `webView` wiring from #1235 rides on hostCall-shaped plumbing — same hang class.

Web worker + QuickJS engines dispatch all channels, which is why browser preview and the CLI never showed it. Bridge traffic stats on the phone confirmed it: zero `__jsr_host_call` across every 15 s window while RAF kept ticking.

## Fix (already upstream)

flutter_js_widget_runtime commit `9d57570`: `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` (union of the sync+async handler maps) is now the single source of truth and the flutter_js engine derives its `setupBridge` list from it; regression test asserts every channel sent by the bootstrap is dispatched. All quality gates green.

## Acceptance

- pubspec override ref updated (or switched to hosted `^0.4.156`), `flutter pub get`, lockfile committed.
- On an iOS/macOS build: `voxel-sandbox` renders (no spinner), `fa-craft` bridge stats show `__jsr_host_call` ≈ RAF counts and gameplay is smooth (native voxel path).

Assignee: ai-teammate (assign via UI if CLI fails).

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1341` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +97

- **Created**: 2026-10-07T05:15:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-07T05:29:40Z

## PR Description

Closes #1341
### What changed
Switched `flutter_app`'s `js_widget_runtime` from the git pin `bd1e7c2` (0.4.154) to **hosted `^0.4.156`** — v0.4.156 = upstream `9d57570` (flutter_js bridge registers every `__jsr_*` channel via `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels`), so `jsr.hostCall`/`jsr.capture` no longer hang on JSC (iOS/macOS voxel spinner, fa-craft scene3d fallback). # gh-1341: Bump js_widget_runtime pin to 9d57570 / ^0.4.156 — flutter_js hostCall/capture channel fix (fa-craft lag, voxel-sandbox spinner)

## Description

## What

The pubspec git-override currently pins js_widget_runtime at `bd1e7c2`. Move it to **`9d57570`** (or hosted `^0.4.156` once CI publishes).

## Why (root cause of the mobile fa-craft/voxel-sandbox reports)

The flutter_js engine registered a hand-maintained `_bridgeChannels` list that was never updated when `__jsr_host_call` and `__jsr_capture` landed. flutter_js delivers `sendMessage` only to channels registered via `setupBridge` — messages on unregistered channels are silently dropped, so every `jsr.hostCall(...)` / `jsr.capture(...)` promise **hung forever** on JSC builds (the app uses FlutterJsWidgetEngineBackend / JavascriptCoreRuntime on iOS+macOS):

- `voxel-sandbox`: first render gated behind the `voxel.attach` probe promise → **infinite spinner**;
- `fa-craft`: probe hangs → `nativeOn` stays null → permanent legacy scene3d fallback (full chunk mesh JSON re-sent every frame) → ~2 FPS and 16x mosaic-subdivided faces;
- the `jsr.openUrl` / `webView` wiring from #1235 rides on hostCall-shaped plumbing — same hang class.

Web worker + QuickJS engines dispatch all channels, which is why browser preview and the CLI never showed it. Bridge traffic stats on the phone confirmed it: zero `__jsr_host_call` across every 15 s window while RAF kept ticking.

## Fix (already upstream)

flutter_js_widget_runtime commit `9d57570`: `JsWidgetBridge.handledChannels` (union of the sync+async handler maps) is now the single source of truth and the flutter_js engine derives its `setupBridge` list from it; regression test asserts every channel sent by the bootstrap is dispatched. All quality gates green.

## Acceptance

- pubspec override ref updated (or switched to hosted `^0.4.156`), `flutter pub get`, lockfile committed.
- On an iOS/macOS build: `voxel-sandbox` renders (no spinner), `fa-craft` bridge stats show `__jsr_host_call` ≈ RAF counts and gameplay is smooth (native voxel path).

Assignee: ai-teammate (assign via UI if CLI fails).

environment:
  sdk: ^3.12.2

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  # The local flutter_agent_harness package (pure Dart core + dart:io env).
  flutter_agent_harness:
    path: ../

  # The local fa_ui package: the Fa theme + provider/model settings widgets.
  fa_ui:
    path: ../packages/fa_ui
  # The extension panel's worker-relay transports + protocol (issue #34).
  # Path dep: fa_browser_agent ships inside the repo's browser_ext/ and is
  # compiled into the SW separately; the app only shares the wire types.
  fa_browser_agent:
    path: ../browser_ext/dart


  # The Office add-in bridge (issue #182): the outlook taskpane bundle

  fa_office_agent:
    path: ../office_addin/dart

    path: ../packages/fa_llm

  fa_hub_client: ^0.2.10

  image: ^4.5.4

  # Load API keys and runtime config from .env for local dev/simulator runs.
  flutter_dotenv: ^6.0.1

  # JS apps platform: runs JavaScript widgets and renders them as native
  # Flutter UI (QuickJS via flutter_js on VM, web worker on web).
  # 0.4.154 ships the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`, >=

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1.
